subject: Post-call recap — Greenline Health: usage trends, blockers, and path to Dedicated/pilot
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Tim Green <tim.green@greenlinehealth.com>, Sarah Li <sarah.li@greenlinehealth.com>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 16:15:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap — Greenline Health: usage trends, blockers, and path to Dedicated/pilot

Hi Tim and Sarah,

Thanks again for taking the time earlier. Quick recap from our side so we’re aligned on pain, measurable goals, and clear next steps.

Key pain points you highlighted:
- Bursty peak latency on nightly batch scoring (15–20 req/s spikes) causing downstream timeouts for the clinical dashboard.
- Rising per-token costs as you scale inference for new triage workflows (costs up ~35% QoQ).
- Need for stronger data residency controls for PHI-adjacent metadata in the EU/US split in Q1.

Stated goals (what success looks like in 90 days):
- Reduce 95th percentile latency by 40% during nightly window.
- Cut unit inference cost by ~20% via batching/quantization and routing.
- Run a 6-week Dedicated pilot for the triage workload to validate latency and cost targets before Q1 rollout.

What we captured on technical scope:
- Primary workload: clinical triage model (long prompt + 2k token responses), synchronous API calls from your scoring service.
- Current monthly active tokens: ~420M; observed nightly peak bursts to ~18k tokens/min. (See attached usage snapshot.)
- Desired SLO: p95 < 350ms for single-turn scoring during production windows.

Agreed next steps:
1) Redwood: share a proposed Dedicated pilot config + cost estimate (Marcus is looped to size infra). Attachment: greenline-usage-snapshot-20261125.csv.
2) Greenline: confirm procurement contact and any mandatory security paperwork timelines (SOC2 + Data Processing Agreement).
3) Joint: schedule a tech walk-through next week for Marcus to review workload traces and KV cache opportunities.

Proposed tentative timeline: pilot kick-off week of Dec 13, 6-week run, decision meeting mid-Jan.

If that all looks right, I’ll route a short SOW draft and a one-page config estimate.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: greenline-usage-snapshot-20261125.csv (usage by endpoint + peak window detail)

Subject: Re: Post-call recap — Greenline Health: usage trends, blockers, and path to Dedicated/pilot

Thanks Hannah — this is helpful and accurate. A couple clarifications from our side:

- The nightly spikes are tied to a new ingest pipeline we deployed last month; we expect them to persist as we onboard two additional clinics in January. So capacity headroom is important.
- Data residency: the triage workflow will store PHI-adjacent metadata in our US tenants for now, but we may route EU patient traffic to EU-only infra in Q1. Can Redwood support a split routing plan for the pilot?
- Procurement: procurement@greenlinehealth.com is our procurement lead (Marta Reyes) — she’ll need a simple statement of work and an invoice schedule.

Two asks:
1) Can you send a ballpark price for a 6-week Dedicated pilot (GPU pool + 99th p95 target) so I can scope budget with Marta?
2) Please include any uplift for an EU region option (we may not enable it for the pilot but need to understand delta).

If you can get an initial config and ballpark numbers by Friday that would be great. We can do the tech walkthrough next Wed (Dec 1) at 10am PT.

—Tim
Tim Green

Subject: Internal: Pilot sizing thoughts for Greenline (draft)

Internal note — quick draft before the walkthrough.

Sizing assumptions (based on Hannah's snapshot + call):
- Base steady-state: ~7k tokens/min; peak burst to 25k tokens/min (business-critical window 02:00–03:30 PT).
- Model: 13B family, medium-sequence (avg 1.6k tokens request/response).

Suggested pilot config:
- Dedicated pool: 4x A100-40GB equiv (or 6x T4 equivalent for cheaper option) with autoscale to +50% on observed queue depth.
- Batching + KV cache enabled for prefix reuse — expect ~22% token cost reduction in steady-state, up to 35% on repeated prompts.
- Quantization: bf16 -> int8 path for the production branch after eval — initial pilot run with mixed precision to validate quality.

Ballpark pricing (6-week pilot):
- A100-equivalent config: $42k total (includes reserved hours + burst capacity).
- Cost-reduced (T4) option: $24k total (higher latency risk on p95).
- EU region add-on: +18% on costs to reserve warm nodes and data egress assumptions.

I’ll flesh these into the SOW and bring benchmarking slides to the Dec 1 tech walkthrough.

Notes/questions for walkthrough:
- Bring sample traces for p95 contributors (padding? long prompt tail?).
- Confirm whether Greenline wants 99th p95 target at pilot (we recommend p95 to start).

Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
